summary: mmdd-doc-mcp probes Alibaba Cloud IMDS and beacons results to hardcoded attacker IP
details: On startup, index.js probes the Alibaba Cloud ECS instance metadata service at 100.100.100.200 — issuing the IMDSv2 PUT /latest/api/token request and querying /latest/meta-data/ram/security-credentials/ — and transmits the reachability results, tagged with the package name, to a hardcoded remote endpoint at 121.199.24.94 (reached as http://121.199.24.94.nip.io with a bare-IP fallback via a TELEMETRY_HOSTS array and a pingTelemetry('?stage=v2probe&src=mmdd-doc-mcp&res=...') call). The destination is wrapped in nip.io wildcard DNS to disguise the bare IP, and comments/identifiers label the behavior as benign 'telemetry' / 'v2 probe' / 'status reporting'. A Markdown documentation MCP tool has no legitimate reason to touch cloud metadata or RAM security-credentials paths on the installer's host; this maps which installers are inside Alibaba Cloud with IMDS reachable and reports that to an attacker-controlled endpoint, enabling follow-on cloud credential theft.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
